lib-inim-prying-eyes.rationale: Lets you see inside a room from touching its wall; inim-1a is 'use one sense at a distance', not memorizing an image already seen (inim-1b) or discerning your own illusions (inim-1c).

lib-inim-discern-own-illusions.rationale: Makes your own illusions transparent but still discernible to you, which is inim-1c's guideline verbatim ('be able to discern your own false images'), not sensing at a distance (inim-1a) or remembering an image (inim-1b).

lib-inim-ear-for-distant-voices.rationale: Hears what is happening at a place reached via Arcane Connection: one sense (hearing) projected at a distance, i.e. inim-1a, not memory of an image (inim-1b) or self-illusion detection (inim-1c).

lib-inim-eyes-eagle.rationale: Sees distant things as if a foot away — inim-3b's guideline gives 'to see clearly at a distance' as its own example, whereas inim-3a is using three separate senses at once, which this spell does not do.

lib-muim-taste-spices-and-herbs.rationale: Makes food or drink taste AND smell as designated — two sensations of the same object changed, matching muim-2a, not muim-2b which converts species from one sense into another (e.g. sound made visible).

lib-peim-invisibility-standing-wizard.rationale: Makes the target invisible, i.e. destroys its ability to affect sight — peim-4a — rather than peim-4b, which destroys any three of taste/touch/smell/hearing but leaves sight untouched.

lib-peim-veil-invisibility.rationale: Makes the target completely undetectable to normal sight regardless of movement — destroying the ability to affect sight is peim-4a; peim-4b covers the non-sight senses instead.

lib-peim-removal-conspicuous-sigil.rationale: Obscures grooves, runes, and markings from sight while shape remains — a sight-only suppression, matching peim-4a ('destroy an object's ability to affect sight') rather than peim-4b's non-sight senses.

lib-peim-silence-smothered-sound.rationale: Makes a being or object incapable of producing sound — hearing is one of the two senses peim-3a covers ('smell or hearing'), whereas peim-3b covers taste and touch, neither of which is sound.

lib-peim-chamber-invisibility.rationale: Causes a Group to become invisible — destroying the ability to affect sight, peim-4a, not peim-4b which destroys three of the other four senses and leaves sight alone.

lib-reim-captive-voice.rationale: Captures a voice and places it inside a bag — the image (of sound) is made to appear contained in another object defined at casting, which is reim-4b verbatim, not reim-4a's simple fifteen-pace relocation.

lib-reim-confusion-insane-vibrations.rationale: Makes everything the target perceives vibrate at high speed and sounds seem to come from the wrong place — objects appearing to move rapidly in a disorientating way is reim-3b's guideline exactly, not reim-3a's flat five-pace repositioning.

lib-reim-image-from-wizard-torn.rationale: The caster's own image separates from his body and, to leave his sight, requires 'an Arcane Connection to yourself... when you cast the spell' that 'becomes an integral part of the image' — matching reim-15a 'make an object appear (to one sense) to be in a location that the caster has an Arcane Connection to' verbatim, not reim-15b's 'summon a disembodied spirit associated with Imaginem': nothing is summoned, the caster's own image is relocated.

lib-inme-thoughts-within-babble.rationale: Lets you understand what speakers meant even when they misuse a language — inme-5b's guideline is 'understand the meaning behind spoken sounds' verbatim, not inme-5a's sensing of a single emotion.

lib-crco-incantation-body-made-whole.rationale: Heals all damage to a human body; crco-35a is 'heal all wounds' verbatim, distinct from resolving a terminal aging crisis (crco-35b) or raising a physical Characteristic (crco-35c).

lib-crte-touch-midas.rationale: Creates a lump of gold, a precious metal — crte-15a's guideline, not crte-15b which repairs an existing crafted item to 'as new' rather than creating raw material.

lib-cran-curse-ravenous-swarm.rationale: Calls a swarm of locusts or destructive insects, matching cran-5b 'create an insect or similar bug' — not cran-5a, which creates an animal product like spidersilk or wool, nor cran-5c, a Recovery-roll bonus.

lib-reme-incantation-summoning-dead.rationale: Calls up a person's ghost, a disembodied spirit associated with Mentem — reme-15b verbatim, not reme-15a which controls a person the caster can currently see (a ghost being summoned is neither present nor visible beforehand).

lib-cran-soothe-pains-beast.rationale: The spell cures one Light Wound suffered by the animal, matching cran-15a's guideline "Heal a Light Wound", not a Recovery bonus (cran-15b), creating a mammal (cran-15c), or forcing maturity (cran-15d).

lib-cran-weavers-trap-webs.rationale: Grows a net of actual spider webs "as thick as string and as strong as iron" — creating the animal product spidersilk, cran-5a's own example, not creating a live insect (cran-5b) or a Recovery bonus (cran-5c).

lib-cran-wizards-mount.rationale: "Creates a horse" — a mammal — matching cran-15c, not healing a Light Wound (cran-15a), a Recovery bonus (cran-15b), or forcing maturity (cran-15d).

lib-inan-shiver-lycanthrope.rationale: Detects whether a person or beast is actually a lycanthrope — learning a specific bodily fact (inan-4b), not sensing the target's dominant emotional drive (inan-4a).

lib-inan-hunters-sense.rationale: Senses the "primary motivations" of every animal within Hearing — inan-4a's 'sense the dominant drive of a beast' in the spell's own words; the shape-sensing it also grants is the level-3 guideline 'get general information about an animal's body', which is what the design line's "+1 for shape and primary motivation" pays for, not inan-4b's 'learn a specific fact about an animal's body' — a silhouette heard at a distance is general information about the body, not a specific fact about it.

lib-muan-beast-outlandish-size.rationale: Changes an animal's Size by +1 while it remains "of huge size" but still recognizably itself, matching muan-4a's 'major change in a beast while leaving it recognizably the same sort of animal' — this changes a live beast, not an animal product (muan-4b).

lib-muan-doublet-impenetrable-silk.rationale: Changes "an item made of animal material — silk, wool, or leather" so it resists cutting, matching muan-4b's 'change something made of animal products in a minor unnatural way' — this affects an animal product, not a live beast (muan-4a).

lib-muan-growth-creeping-things.rationale: Causes a live small creature to grow to four times its size while remaining the same sort of animal — muan-4a's 'major change in a beast while leaving it recognizably the same sort of animal', not muan-4b which only affects animal products.

lib-muan-beast-minuscule-proportions.rationale: Reduces a live animal's Size by 2 while it remains the same beast, just runt-sized — muan-4a's major-but-recognizable change to a beast, not muan-4b's minor change to an animal product.

lib-muan-beast-remade.rationale: "Gives one land beast a human form" with a Corpus requisite exactly as muan-10a specifies ('change an animal into a human... requires a Corpus requisite'), not muan-10b which turns an animal into a plant with a Herbam requisite.

lib-muan-transformation-ravenous-beast-t.rationale: "Turns any animal into a toad" — changing one animal into a different animal, muan-5a verbatim — not a minor unnatural change to the same animal (muan-5b) or a change to an animal product (muan-5c).

lib-muan-steed-vengeance.rationale: Gives a horse fangs, razor-sharp hooves, and steam breath while it remains a horse — muan-15a's own example is 'give a horse claws and fangs', not muan-15b which turns the animal into a non-living item.

lib-pean-decay-fur-and-hide.rationale: Destroys an object made of animal fur or hide, including wool and leather, matching pean-4a's guideline "Destroy something made of animal products", not causing a beast pain (pean-4b) or Fatigue loss (pean-4c).

lib-pean-agony-beast.rationale: The beast "lashes wildly about... and howls in great pain" but only needs a Stamina roll to act, with no wound inflicted — pean-4b's 'cause a beast pain, but do no real damage', not destroying an animal product (pean-4a) or a Fatigue loss (pean-4c).

lib-pean-blunt-vipers-fangs.rationale: Blunts a beast's natural weapons, halving their damage while the beast recovers as from a Light Wound — pean-5a's 'injure an animal so it is hampered, but not damaged (roughly halves effectiveness)', not destroying a corpse (pean-5b) or inflicting an actual Light Wound (pean-5c).

lib-pean-falcons-hood.rationale: "Destroys an animal's vision" — one of a beast's major senses — matching pean-20c, not inflicting an Incapacitating Wound (pean-20a) or severing a limb (pean-20b).

lib-pean-cripple-howling-wolf.rationale: "One of the target's legs breaks cleanly. The animal cannot walk on that leg, but the damage heals as a Medium Wound" matches pean-15c's 'cripple a beast's limb, so that it is unusable but could heal', not destroying a minor sense (pean-15a), inflicting a Heavy Wound outright (pean-15b), or aging (pean-15d).

lib-rean-disguise-putrid-aroma.rationale: Makes a carnivore "take no interest in you" and not attack — rean-2b's 'protect the target from animal attacks (only affects animals without supernatural abilities)', not planting a suggestion (rean-2a) or treating animal-product items (rean-2c).

lib-rean-circle-beast-warding.rationale: Inscribes a circle "that no normal beast will cross" — protecting against attacks by ordinary (non-supernatural) animals, rean-2b, not planting a suggestion in one animal's mind (rean-2a) or treating animal-product items (rean-2c).

lib-rean-panic-elephants-mouse.rationale: "Makes an animal afraid... by preying upon its instinctive fears" — manipulating its emotions, rean-5a — not paralysis (rean-5b), warding (rean-5c), spirit control (rean-5d), or vermin generation (rean-5e).

lib-rean-vipers-gaze.rationale: "Holds an animal rigid as long as you maintain eye contact" is a literal paralysis effect, rean-5b, not emotional manipulation (rean-5a), warding (rean-5c), spirit control (rean-5d), or vermin generation (rean-5e).

lib-rean-gentle-beast.rationale: "Calms an animal, making it nearly fearless... does not resist being ridden, shaved" — making it completely passive, rean-10a — not instantly transporting it (rean-10b).

lib-rean-mastering-unruly-beast.rationale: "You can make an animal perform any act it is capable of" is complete control over the animal, rean-15a, not summoning a disembodied spirit (rean-15b).

lib-rean-commanding-harnessed-beast.rationale: "You implant a complicated command into an animal, which it carries out" is complete control of the beast, rean-15a, not summoning a disembodied spirit (rean-15b).

lib-craq-footsteps-slippery-oil.rationale: Spreads "nonflammable grease" over an uncontained slick area — craq-3a's 'create water (or some other natural liquid) that is not contained', not creating ice (craq-3b).

lib-craq-creeping-oil.rationale: Saturates cloth with a spot of flammable oil that spreads over the target — creating an uncontained natural liquid, craq-3a, not creating ice (craq-3b).

lib-craq-mighty-torrent-water.rationale: A "jet of water" that knocks the target back with force is a high-flow-rate geyser, craq-10a, not a created poison (craq-10b) — the damage comes from impact, not toxicity.

lib-muaq-incantation-putrid-wine.rationale: Makes liquids in the room "vile, and malodorous" with no wound or damage effect described — changing one natural liquid into another (muaq-2a), not turning it into a poison that causes a Light Wound (muaq-2b).

lib-muaq-lungs-fish.rationale: "Turns water into air" with an explicit Auram requisite — muaq-4a's 'change a liquid into an unrelated solid or gas (with requisites)' verbatim — not splitting a liquid into two liquids (muaq-4b), poisoning (muaq-4c), or an unnatural liquid (muaq-4d).

lib-muaq-vile-water-sterility.rationale: The spell's own design line calls its base effect "a very unnatural liquid", matching muaq-4d verbatim, not a solid/gas change (muaq-4a), splitting into two liquids (muaq-4b), or poisoning (muaq-4c).

lib-reaq-push-gentle-wave.rationale: Forms a wave to "propel a small boat slowly through the water" via ongoing pushing, matching reaq-4a's 'control a liquid in a forceful but calm way, such as a fast but constant current', not reaq-4b's instantaneous transport.

lib-reaq-chaos-angry-waves.rationale: "Causes water to churn wildly, overturning small water craft" is violent control of ordinary water, reaq-5b, not warding against water (reaq-5a), spirit control (reaq-5c), or controlling a water elemental (reaq-5d).

lib-crau-jupiters-resounding-blow.rationale: Creates a thunderclap loud enough to deafen bystanders, matching crau-3a's example of 'deafening thunder' as a severe weather phenomenon, not crau-3b's debilitating air (stench, poison).

lib-crau-stench-twenty-corpses.rationale: Creates a horrible stench that forces Stamina rolls or a penalty and vomiting, i.e. a debilitating kind of air (crau-3b's 'noxious stench'), not a weather phenomenon like thunder or wind (crau-3a).

lib-crau-wreaths-foul-smoke.rationale: Thick sulfurous smoke that causes Fatigue loss and Light Wounds on repeated exposure is a debilitating kind of air (crau-3b), not a severe weather phenomenon like thunder, rain, or wind (crau-3a).

lib-crau-broom-winds.rationale: Whips up violent, gale-strength winds strong enough to knock a target down, matching crau-3a's 'gale force wind' as a severe weather phenomenon, not crau-3b's debilitating air.

lib-crau-charge-angry-winds.rationale: A roaring wall of wind that knocks people down and defeats missile fire is crau-3a's 'gale force wind' severe weather phenomenon, not crau-3b's debilitating air.

lib-crau-circling-winds-protection.rationale: Surrounds the caster with winds circling at great speed, a localized gale-force wind (crau-3a's severe weather phenomenon), with a separate Rego requisite layered on for the defensive control; not crau-3b's debilitating air.

lib-crau-clouds-rain-and-thunder.rationale: Creates a small but severe rainstorm with lightning and winds, matching crau-3a's 'monsoon rain'/'deafening thunder' severe weather phenomenon, not crau-3b's debilitating air.

lib-inau-sailors-foretaste-morrow.rationale: Gives the caster an extrapolated, occasionally-wrong prediction of tomorrow's weather — an intuition about the air's future state (inau-4b), not direct sensing of the air's current mundane properties (inau-4a).

lib-inau-eyes-bat.rationale: Lets the caster sense the boundaries of the air itself (where solid objects are) to navigate in darkness — a direct mundane property of the air (inau-4a), not an intuited fact (inau-4b).

lib-muau-rain-stones.rationale: Turns rain into stones as it falls, with a Terram requisite for the specific solid — muau-4a's 'transform an amount of air into another element (fire, earth, or water)', not muau-4b's harmful-gas Light Wound effect.

lib-muau-talons-winds.rationale: Transforms a wind into an abrasive medium that cuts for +4 damage, i.e. turning a gas into a harmful form that inflicts a Light Wound (muau-4b), not an elemental transformation into fire/earth/water (muau-4a).

lib-muau-rain-oil.rationale: Turns rain into droplets of oil, with an Aquam requisite for the specific liquid — muau-4a's 'transform an amount of air into another element ... water', not muau-4b's harmful-gas wound effect.

lib-peau-cloudless-sky-returned.rationale: Clears the sky of clouds and other meteorological activity, matching peau-10a's destruction of a severe weather phenomenon, not peau-10b's debilitating kind of air (stench, poison).

lib-reau-ward-against-rain.rationale: Wards the caster so no rain falls on them no matter the weather — reau-4b's 'ward someone against a type of normal weather phenomenon', not reau-4a's active control of a severe phenomenon.

lib-reau-clouds-thunderous-might.rationale: Gathers pre-existing clouds and winds into a storm under the caster's ongoing control, matching reau-4a's 'control a severe weather phenomenon', not reau-4b's defensive ward.

lib-reau-gathering-stormy-might.rationale: As Clouds of Thunderous Might but covering the whole visible sky, still under the caster's control — reau-4a's 'control a severe weather phenomenon', not reau-4b's ward.

lib-invi-sense-magical-power.rationale: Tells the caster only whether he is currently standing in a Magic aura, matching invi-1b's 'detect presence of supernatural aura', not detecting high-magnitude magic (invi-1a) or vis (invi-1c).

lib-invi-scales-magical-weight.rationale: Compares an unknown quantity of vis against a known amount to determine how many pawns are present, matching invi-4b's 'judge amount of vis present', not detecting magic strength (invi-4a) or discerning vis's Art (invi-4c).

lib-invi-sense-nature-vis.rationale: Reveals which Art (Technique or Form) a supply of raw vis is associated with via its glowing color, matching invi-4c's 'discern the Art of vis', not judging quantity (invi-4b) or detecting magic strength (invi-4a).

lib-invi-piercing-faerie-veil.rationale: Lets the caster see through the boundary of a Faerie regio to find the path to the next level, matching invi-3b's 'detect regio boundaries', not invi-3a's detection of magic strength.

lib-crco-bind-wound.rationale: Seals the target's wounds so they cannot worsen but does not speed recovery, matching crco-3b 'prevent all of a target's wounds from getting any worse' rather than crco-3a's Recovery-roll bonus.

lib-crco-charm-against-putrefaction.rationale: Prevents decay of a human corpse or severed body part, matching crco-2b 'preserve a corpse from decay' rather than crco-2a's Recovery-roll bonus, which applies to the living.

lib-crco-chirurgeons-healing-touch.rationale: Heals a single Light Wound from injury and explicitly does not heal poison or disease, matching crco-15a 'heal a Light Wound' rather than the Recovery bonus (crco-15b) or aging-crisis (crco-15c) guidelines.

lib-crco-gentle-touch-purified-body.rationale: Cures a Light-Wound-equivalent affliction caused by poison or disease (not injury), the disease/poison counterpart to Chirurgeon's Healing Touch built on the same 'heal a Light Wound' severity guideline (crco-15a), not the Recovery bonus (crco-15b) or aging crisis (crco-15c).

lib-crco-restoration-defiled-body.rationale: Explicitly 'does not heal wounds, only extra effects,' removing crippling after-effects of injury, poison, or disease, matching crco-20b rather than crco-20a (Medium Wound); the passing mention of premature aging never uses the book's 'aging crisis' terminology (crco-20c).

lib-crco-severed-limb-made-whole.rationale: Reattaches a limb that has been detached from the body, matching crco-25c 'restore a lost limb' — the design line's -1 "because the old limb is needed" is a discount on precisely that guideline. A missing limb is not a wound (Incantation of the Body Made Whole can heal "only wounds, not such damage as missing limbs"), so this is neither crco-25a's Heavy Wound nor crco-25b's across-the-board improvement of wound severity, and no aging crisis is involved (crco-25d).

lib-crco-cheating-reaper.rationale: Resolves 'a major (or less severe) crisis caused by aging,' matching crco-25d 'resolve a major aging crisis' verbatim, not the wound-healing (crco-25a), wound-severity-improvement (crco-25b), or limb-restoration (crco-25c) guidelines.

lib-inco-revealed-flaws-mortal-flesh.rationale: Finds medical defects in a touched, living person, matching inco-5a 'sense a specific piece of information about a body' rather than inco-5b's speaking with a corpse.

lib-inco-whispers-through-black-gate.rationale: Lets the caster converse with an undecayed corpse's spirit through the barrier between the dead and living, matching inco-5b 'speak with a dead body' rather than inco-5a's sensing information about a body.

lib-muco-disguise-new-visage.rationale: Transforms the target's facial features to another human configuration, matching muco-3a's changing a person's appearance while remaining human in form, not muco-3b's transformation of non-living human bone.

lib-muco-preternatural-growth-and-shrink.rationale: Changes the target's Size up by one point or down by two while he remains an ordinary human, matching muco-3a's 'utterly change the appearance or size of a person (though they must still remain human in form)' — the size clause verbatim, with the extra magnitude buying the choice of three outcomes rather than a different guideline. Nothing is done to non-living bone (muco-3b).

lib-muco-arm-infant.rationale: Shrinks a person's arm and changes its proportions while it remains a living human arm, matching muco-3a's change to a person's appearance/size, not muco-3b's change to non-living bone.

lib-muco-shape-woodland-prowler.rationale: Changes the target into a wolf, matching muco-10a 'turn a human into a land animal' rather than muco-10b's Soak bonus.

lib-muco-cloak-black-feathers.rationale: Transforms the caster into a raven, matching muco-20a 'turn a human into a bird or a fish' rather than muco-20b's Soak bonus.

lib-muco-curse-circe.rationale: Turns a person into a pig, matching muco-10a 'turn a human into a land animal' rather than muco-10b's Soak bonus.

lib-muco-stance-patient-tree.rationale: Turns the caster into a living tree that senses day/night and wind, matching muco-25c 'turn a human into a plant' rather than a transformation into a solid inanimate object (muco-25a) or a Soak bonus (muco-25b).

lib-muco-silent-vigil.rationale: The caster becomes part of a rock formation, and the spell is printed with Req: Terram exactly as muco-25a specifies ('turn a human into a solid inanimate object', Terram requisite); the retained hearing and the ability to step back out are what the design line's "+1 for special effect" buys. The spell grants no Soak at all (muco-25b), and a transformation into a plant would carry a Herbam requisite rather than a Terram one (muco-25c).

lib-peco-dust-to-dust.rationale: Turns a dead body to dust, matching peco-5b 'destroy a corpse' rather than inflicting a Light Wound (peco-5a) or hampering a living target (peco-5c).

lib-peco-wound-that-weeps.rationale: Opens a bleeding wound on a living target described as 'only a Light Wound,' matching peco-5a 'inflict a Light Wound' rather than destroying a corpse (peco-5b) or a non-injuring hampering effect (peco-5c).

lib-peco-invocation-weariness.rationale: Causes the target to lose a Fatigue level rather than inflicting an actual wound, matching peco-10b rather than peco-10a's Medium Wound.

lib-peco-bane-decrepit-body.rationale: Ages the target 5 years, matching peco-15a 'age someone by up to five years' verbatim, not the limb-crippling (peco-15b), minor-sense-destruction (peco-15c), or Heavy Wound (peco-15d) guidelines.

lib-peco-curse-leprous-flesh.rationale: Inflicts leprosy, a disease that rots the target's flesh over weeks, matching peco-20b 'inflict a major disease' rather than destroying a sense (peco-20a), severing a limb (peco-20c), or a direct Incapacitating Wound (peco-20d) — its wound-equivalent severity is just the disease's mechanical effect, not a separate guideline.

lib-peco-grip-choking-hand.rationale: Constricts the target's throat, draining a Fatigue level each round rather than wounding them, matching peco-10b rather than peco-10a's Medium Wound.

lib-peco-incantation-milky-eyes.rationale: Blinds the target with cataracts and explicitly 'heals as a Heavy Wound,' matching peco-20a 'destroy one of a person's major senses (heals as a Heavy Wound)' verbatim, not disease (peco-20b), limb-severing (peco-20c), or a direct Incapacitating Wound (peco-20d).

lib-peco-twist-tongue.rationale: The spell twists the tongue so it cannot function, and the damage 'heals as a Medium Wound' -- a body part rendered unusable but capable of healing, which is peco-15b's structure word for word ('Cripple a limb, making it unusable but still capable of healing (heals as a Medium Wound)'). The 'heals as a Medium Wound' clause does not discriminate, since peco-15c carries it too. What discriminates is that the spell destroys the ability to *speak*, and speech is not a sense: peco-15c destroys 'one of a person's minor senses', and the spell says nothing about taste or any other perception. Both readings stretch a word -- a tongue is not a limb either -- but the smaller stretch is the one that matches what the spell actually does to the body. Corrected under item 32.2 after a blind model pass flagged it; the entry previously read peco-15c, rejecting peco-15b only on 'the tongue is not a limb' without weighing that speech is not a sense.

lib-peco-curse-unportended-plague.rationale: Starts a plague afflicting everyone in the boundary with 'the disease' described under Curse of the Leprous Flesh, matching peco-20b 'inflict a major disease' for the same reason as that spell.

lib-reco-rise-feathery-body.rationale: Lets the target float straight up to any height but explicitly cannot move horizontally, matching reco-4c 'move a target slowly straight up' rather than movement in any direction (reco-4b) or general large-scale movement control (reco-4a).

lib-reco-despair-quivering-manacles.rationale: Makes the target shake vigorously in place, imposing penalties on their actions rather than relocating them, matching reco-4a 'control the large-scale physical movements of a target' rather than the directional-movement guidelines (reco-4b, reco-4c).

lib-reco-endurance-berserkers.rationale: Makes the caster's body act as though unwounded and unfatigued, matching reco-10b 'eliminate the penalties of Fatigue and wounds' verbatim, not the motion-control, corpse-animation, transport, or surgery guidelines.

lib-reco-gift-frogs-legs.rationale: Grants the target an enhanced leap requiring their own landing roll rather than instantly relocating them, matching reco-10a 'control a target's motions' rather than the instant 5-pace transport (reco-10d), which does not fit a jump covering up to 25 feet that takes real time to land.

lib-reco-lifting-dangling-puppet.rationale: Lifts a person straight up (or lets them descend) through the air, matching reco-4c 'move a target slowly straight up, or in one direction over surfaces that cannot support it' rather than movement in any direction (reco-4b) or general movement control (reco-4a).

lib-reco-gift-vigor.rationale: Transfers bodily Fatigue energy from the caster to the target, matching reco-15a 'direct the flow of bodily energy' verbatim, not the directional-movement, spirit-summoning, transport, warding, or surgery guidelines.

lib-reco-awaken-slumbering-corpse.rationale: Causes a corpse to function and obey simple verbal commands, matching reco-10c 'animate a corpse' verbatim, not the motion-control, fatigue/wound-elimination, transport, or surgery guidelines.

lib-reco-strings-unwilling-marionette.rationale: Lets the caster control a living person's physical movements such as walking and turning, matching reco-10a 'control a target's motions' rather than animating a corpse (reco-10c) or the other level-10 guidelines.

lib-reco-walking-corpse.rationale: Turns a corpse into a servant that follows simple verbal commands, matching reco-10c 'animate a corpse' verbatim, not the motion-control, fatigue/wound-elimination, transport, or surgery guidelines.

lib-crhe-conjure-sturdy-vine.rationale: Grows an entirely new 10-pace vine from a quantity of wood or fertile soil, matching crhe-1c 'create a plant' — not crhe-1a, whose guideline is for sustaining an already-existing plant's growth, not conjuring new plant matter.

lib-crhe-trap-entwining-vines.rationale: Causes new woody vines to grow rapidly from fertile earth to ensnare a target, matching crhe-1c 'create a plant' rather than crhe-1a's guideline for nursing an existing plant's growth over the spell's duration.

lib-crhe-bridge-wood.rationale: Creates a bridge of living leaves, vines, and wood, matching crhe-3a's guideline example verbatim ('such as a living wall or bridge'), not crhe-3b's plant-healing effect.

lib-crhe-wall-thorns.rationale: Instantly grows a wall of thorny bushes out of existing bushes or fertile soil — new plant matter, not accelerated growth of a designated existing plant — matching crhe-1c 'create a plant', not crhe-1a.

lib-crhe-wall-living-wood.rationale: Grows a straight wall of living oak from nearby trees or fertile earth, matching crhe-3a's guideline example verbatim ('such as a living wall or bridge'), not crhe-3b's plant-healing effect.

lib-muhe-rope-bronze.rationale: Printed with Req: Terram, and turns plant-material rope into bronze, matching muhe-4a 'change a plant or item made from plant products into metal or stone (Terram requisite)', not muhe-4b's Mentem-requisite consciousness effect.

lib-muhe-thaumaturgical-transformation-p.rationale: Printed with Req: Terram, and makes plant material as hard as iron, matching muhe-4a's metal/stone transformation with Terram requisite, not muhe-4b's awaken-consciousness effect.

lib-muhe-stir-slumbering-tree.rationale: Printed with Req: Mentem, and raises a tree to a human-like consciousness that can see and hear, matching muhe-4b 'awaken the consciousness of a plant (Mentem requisite)', not muhe-4a's metal/stone transformation.

lib-muhe-curse-haunted-forest.rationale: Turns a forest's trees conscious and cruel, capable of sight, hearing, and limited movement, matching muhe-4b 'awaken the consciousness of a plant' — not muhe-4a's metal/stone transformation, which does not occur here (the printed Req: Perdo covers the trees' gnarled, hideous appearance, a separate effect bundled at no extra cost).

lib-rehe-dance-staves.rationale: Animates a pole, staff, or haft — explicitly 'any other long, thin, non-living wooden object', i.e. a crafted implement — matching rehe-3b 'manipulate items made of plant products', not rehe-3a's guideline for controlling raw, unworked wood.

lib-rehe-repel-wooden-shafts.rationale: Deflects a single blow from any weapon made of wood, matching rehe-4a 'deflect a single attack by a wooden weapon' verbatim, not rehe-4b (moving a rooted plant) or rehe-4c (treating plant-product items).

lib-rehe-strike-angered-branch.rationale: Animates a natural tree branch to swing and strike a target, matching rehe-3a 'control an amount of wood' (raw wood), not rehe-3b's guideline for manipulating crafted plant-product items.

lib-rehe-tangle-wood-and-thorns.rationale: Hurls and animates a designated length of raw wood (possibly thorny) to ensnare a target, matching rehe-3a 'control an amount of wood', not rehe-3b's crafted-item guideline.

lib-rehe-coils-entangling-plants.rationale: Animates living grass and small plants in a field to grab and entangle targets, matching rehe-3a 'control an amount of wood' (the guideline header notes living and dead wood are equally easy to control), not rehe-3b's crafted-item guideline.

lib-rehe-lord-trees.rationale: Moves a tree's branches and bends its trunk while the tree stays rooted in place, matching rehe-4b 'control an entire plant... although it remains rooted' — confirmed by the level-30 'Freeing the Striding Tree' being explicitly 'Like Lord of the Trees, above, but the tree can walk', which needs the higher-level 'need not remain rooted' guideline instead.

lib-rehe-treacherous-spear.rationale: Animates a wooden weapon to attack its wielder on its own, without requiring the caster's continued control, matching rehe-10a 'move with purpose and intelligence, without requiring your constant control', not rehe-10b's plant-transport guideline (nothing is transported).

lib-rehe-twist-living-tree.rationale: Bends a living tree into a cage, shelter, or wall while it stays rooted, matching rehe-4b 'control an entire plant... although it remains rooted', not rehe-4a (deflecting a weapon) or rehe-4c (treating plant-product items).

lib-rehe-ward-against-wood.rationale: Protects the caster so that nonenchanted wood cannot touch his body, matching rehe-15a 'ward someone against mundane plant products' verbatim, not the other level-15 guidelines (blossoming trees, weaving, spirit-summoning).

lib-rehe-freeing-striding-tree.rationale: Explicitly described as 'Like Lord of the Trees, above, but the tree can walk', matching rehe-5a 'moving it around as you direct, and it need not remain rooted' — the walking is exactly what distinguishes it from the level-4 rooted version.

lib-rehe-calling-council-trees.rationale: Calls all magical, potentially mobile trees within the woodland to come to the ritual site, matching rehe-5c 'summon a mobile plant', not rehe-5b's disembodied-spirit guideline — these are living trees, not spirits.

lib-inte-eyes-eons.rationale: Determines the age of a nonliving target to within 10% of its actual age — a single mundane fact about an object — matching inte-4a 'learn one mundane property of an object', not inte-4b's sight-based guideline (no seeing is involved).

lib-inte-stone-tell-mind-that-sits.rationale: Lets the caster talk with natural stone, matching inte-20c 'speak with a natural rock (e.g., a boulder)' verbatim, not inte-20a (learning magical properties) or inte-20b (seeing through earth).

lib-inte-dream-mind-that-sits.rationale: Probes and communes with a spirit inside a natural stone object over many hours, matching inte-30a 'commune with a natural rock', not inte-30b's metal-object guideline (no metal is involved).

lib-mute-supple-iron-and-rigid-rope.rationale: Makes a stiff object flexible or a flexible object stiff, using casting requisites appropriate to the material, matching mute-3a 'change dirt to be slightly unnatural (may require requisites)' verbatim — no material-category change (liquid/gas or stone) occurs.

lib-mute-edge-razor.rationale: Sharpens a metal edge to a degree unequaled by manual methods, matching mute-3a 'change dirt to be slightly unnatural' — the metal stays metal, only its sharpness property changes unnaturally, unlike mute-3b/c's material-category changes.

lib-mute-object-increased-size.rationale: Doubles an inanimate object's dimensions (and hence roughly its order of magnitude in volume), matching mute-4d 'make something grow to ten times its previous volume' verbatim, not the material-composition guidelines (mute-4a/b/c), since no material change occurs.

lib-mute-teeth-earth-mother.rationale: Turns the ground into twenty pillars of white marble — dirt changed to stone, mute-3c verbatim, the guideline already carrying the one magnitude the Muto Terram introduction charges 'to change to or from stone or glass' (hence base 3 where the earth-to-earth change is base 2). The marble is ordinary marble, so the material itself is not unnatural (mute-3a) — the spear-point shape and circular arrangement are what the "+2 fancy effect" pays for — and no liquid or gas is produced (mute-3b).

lib-rete-unseen-arm.rationale: Slowly moves a nonliving thing like a mug, instrument, or pouch of coins at a distance, matching rete-2a 'control or move dirt in a slightly unnatural fashion', not rete-2b (keeping dirt away) or rete-2c (shaping/forming dirt).

lib-rete-trackless-step.rationale: The target leaves no tracks at all while he keeps moving, and the spell lapses the moment he stops — the earth is held off him for as long as he is attending to it, which is rete-2b's 'keep dirt away from you, under your conscious control (that is, you must be aware of its presence)', the limited form of the level-5 'keep all dirt away from your body'. The Duration is printed as "Special (based on Concentration)", that conscious control expressed as a Duration. The spell prevents tracks rather than erasing them, so no dirt is moved unnaturally back into place (rete-2a), and nothing is worked into a shape (rete-2c, which The Forgiving Earth and The Unyielding Earth use).

lib-rete-invisible-sling-vilano.rationale: Hurls a stone that inflicts +5 damage with a 20-pace range increment, matching rete-5d 'hurl a hard projectile with enough force to do +5 damage (range increment of 20 paces)' verbatim, not the other level-5 guidelines (warding, spirits, elementals).

lib-rete-forgiving-earth.rationale: Loosens packed dirt into ground as loose as plowed earth, matching rete-2c 'shape and form dirt, as if a craftsman had worked it', not rete-2a (moving dirt elsewhere) or rete-2b (warding dirt away).

lib-rete-unyielding-earth.rationale: Compacts loose ground into solid packed dirt, matching rete-2c 'shape and form dirt, as if a craftsman had worked it', not rete-2a (moving dirt elsewhere) or rete-2b (warding dirt away).

lib-crig-palm-flame.rationale: A flame conjured in the palm that 'can ignite very flammable items' matches crig-3c; the spell's total level (Base 3 + Touch + Conc, no extra magnitude) pays for only one base-3 effect, and the torch-like light is the unavoidable physical byproduct of a real flame, not a separately-paid crig-3a light effect — contrast Lamp without Flame, which explicitly buys light with 'no apparent source' (i.e. light without real fire, the case crig-3a actually covers). Nothing chills/heats the caster's own hand (ruling out crig-3b).

lib-crig-heat-searing-forge.rationale: Two guidelines at once, both level 4, so the spell pays for one. crig-4a ('Create a fire doing +5 damage') is the primary baseEffectId: the spell states +5 damage for a breastplate-sized object in contact for a round, the ladder's own figure. crig-4d ('Heat an object enough to boil water') is recorded as a magnitude-0 adjustment (extract_spells.COMBINED_BASE_EFFECTS): the spell's first sentence is 'Heats a piece of metal so that it is too hot to touch', which is hotter than level 3's 'hot to the touch' and cooler than level 5's 'glow red-hot' -- boiling point, exactly crig-4d. The heat row at level 3 would also combine for free, being lower, but it understates a metal that burns on contact. This entry has been argued both ways: it read crig-4a on the damage figure alone, then crig-4d on the ladder structure alone. Neither was complete -- the spell genuinely does both, and the Requisites section's 'the base Arts and level for the spell are those for the highest-level effect it has' (Core Rules line 12372) is what makes the second free. Settled under item 32.2.

lib-crig-lamp-without-flame.rationale: Creates 'a steady light as bright as daylight on a cloudy day' with 'no apparent source' (no real fire at all), matching crig-4b's 'Create light as bright as a cloudy day' precisely.

lib-crig-blade-virulent-flame.rationale: Forms a fire along a blade doing '+5' (or double, whichever is greater), matching crig-5b's 'fire doing +5 damage in an unnatural shape... covering an item' (the blade being the covered item), not the +10-damage crig-5a.

lib-crig-flash-scarlet-flames.rationale: The flash is explicitly 'equivalent to looking straight at the sun,' matching crig-5c's 'Create light as bright as direct sunlight on a clear day' exactly.

lib-crig-pilum-fire.rationale: The jet of fire does exactly '+15 damage' to its target, the figure from crig-10a ('Create a fire doing +15 damage'), not the +10-in-unnatural-shape crig-10b.

lib-crig-arc-fiery-ribbons.rationale: The ribbons of flame do '+10 damage' to everyone in the arc, matching crig-5a's 'Create a fire doing +10 damage' by its damage figure, not the +5-damage unnatural-shape guideline crig-5b.

lib-crig-coat-flame.rationale: The target is 'swathed in fire' taking '+5 damage every round,' matching crig-5b's 'fire doing +5 damage in an unnatural shape, such as in a ring or sheet' (a fire-sheet coating the wearer), not the +10-damage crig-5a.

lib-crig-circle-encompassing-flames.rationale: The ring of flames deals exactly '+20 damage' to anyone passing through it, matching crig-20b's 'fire doing +20 damage in an unnatural shape' (a ring), not the +25-damage crig-20a.

lib-inig-tales-ashes.rationale: Reveals what specific touched ashes originally were and how they burned, i.e. the mundane properties of that ash (inig-3a), not a general area-wide search for past fire traces (inig-3b).

lib-inig-shadows-fires-past.rationale: Lets you 'see where fires have been in the past lunar month' and explicitly 'detects the traces of fire,' matching inig-3b's guideline wording ('Detect the traces of fires which burned within the last lunar month') verbatim, rather than reading properties of a specific pile of ash (inig-3a).

lib-inig-vision-heats-light.rationale: Lets you see the heat of any object at body temperature or hotter (not specifically 'a fire'), matching inig-2d's 'Sense levels of heat,' unlike inig-2a/2b/2c which are all scoped to detecting fires specifically.

lib-peig-conjuration-indubitable-cold.rationale: The spell achieves all three Perdo Ignem level-4 guidelines at once, and pays for one. Its own text does each in turn: 'all nonliving things are chilled thoroughly' (peig-4b, chill an object), 'all living things ... lose one Fatigue level' (peig-4c), and 'campfires and smaller fires go out' (peig-4a, extinguish a fire) -- the Ignem base Individual is 'a large campfire' (Core Rules line 14260), so an Individual-sized fire is exactly what a base-4 extinguish reaches. Larger fires are only reduced because destroying a more intense one costs one magnitude per five points of damage above +5 (line 14461), which this spell does not spend. peig-4b is recorded as the primary baseEffectId and the other two as magnitude-0 adjustments (extract_spells.COMBINED_BASE_EFFECTS); which is called primary is cosmetic, since all three are level 4. The rule they rest on is the Requisites section's 'the base Arts and level for the spell are those for the highest-level effect it has' (line 12372), stated there for an added Art and extended here to same-Art guidelines. Corrected under item 32.2: this entry previously recorded only peig-4c as combined and argued peig-4a away as a consequence of the chill -- but air at slightly below freezing does not put out a campfire, so the extinguishing is a separate effect, not a byproduct.

lib-peig-winters-icy-touch.rationale: 'The target loses a Fatigue level' is peig-4c's guideline verbatim ('Chill a person so that they lose a Fatigue level'), not extinguishing a fire (peig-4a) or chilling an inanimate object (peig-4b).

lib-peig-well-without-light.rationale: 'Removes light from the target structure' until the entire area is dark, matching peig-3a's 'Completely extinguish all light in an area,' not the partial fire-reduction of peig-3b.

lib-reig-tremulous-vault-torchs-flame.rationale: The fire 'make[s] a leap of up to 10 feet' via a Targeting roll, a discrete instantaneous relocation matching reig-3c's 'Transport a fire instantly up to 5 paces,' not the gradual/continuous movement of reig-3b.

lib-reig-leap-fire.rationale: Shares the same discrete leap-and-Targeting-roll mechanic as Tremulous Vault of the Torch's Flame, matching reig-3c's instantaneous transport, not the continuous 'move a fire quickly' of reig-3b.

lib-reig-light-shaft-night.rationale: Gathers ambient moonbeams/starlight into a shaft that 'moves under your control,' matching reig-3a's 'Control a fire [or, per the Rego Ignem intro, light] in a natural fashion (for example, control its direction of spread),' not an instantaneous transport (reig-3c) or fire left burning naturally elsewhere (reig-3b).

lib-crme-panic-trembling-heart.rationale: Creates an overpowering fear of a specific object/person/place in the target's mind, matching crme-4a 'Put a thought or emotion into another's mind' - not crme-4b, which restores an existing memory from a fragment.

lib-crme-rising-ire.rationale: Makes the target furious at someone or something of the caster's choice - implanting an emotion, matching crme-4a 'Put a thought or emotion into another's mind', not crme-4b's memory restoration.

lib-crme-memory-distant-dream.rationale: Inserts a full and complete memory into a person's mind from nothing, matching crme-5a 'Create a memory in another's mind' - not crme-5b, which requires a fragment of an existing memory to restore.

lib-crme-pains-perpetual-worry.rationale: Gives the target a nagging, painful anxious emotion out of nowhere, matching crme-4a 'Put a thought or emotion into another's mind', not crme-4b's memory restoration.

lib-crme-weight-thousand-hells.rationale: Makes the victim feel "the despair, anguish, pain, and sorrow of a thousand sinners in Hell" — an emotion placed into another's mind out of nothing, crme-4a, with the design line's "+1 complex effect" paying for the Personality Trait and concentration penalties that follow. Nothing of the target's own is recovered from a surviving fragment, which is all crme-4b does.

lib-inme-sight-transparent-motive.rationale: Detects the single general motive (fear, anger, greed) most powerfully influencing the target, matching inme-5a 'Sense a single emotion in a being' - not inme-5b, which is about understanding spoken sounds/language.

lib-inme-perception-conflicting-motives.rationale: Detects the conflicting motives (e.g. fear vs. duty) behind a target's actions - sensing the target's emotions, matching inme-10a 'Sense all of the emotions in a being', not inme-10b's truth-of-a-statement guideline.

lib-inme-posing-silent-question.rationale: Asks one silent mental question and detects the answer the target believes - matching inme-15c 'Pick a single answer from the mind of a target' precisely, not inme-15a's general two-way speech or inme-15b's broader surface-thought reading.

lib-mume-mind-beast.rationale: Turns the target's mind into that of an animal (Req: Animal) - a total transformation of the mind, matching mume-15b 'Utterly change a person's mind', not mume-15a, which requires an Imaginem requisite this spell doesn't carry.

lib-mume-vision-haunting-spirits.rationale: Makes all spirits in the area visible, with an explicit Req: Imaginem matching mume-15a's own 'Imaginem requisite' notation exactly - not mume-15b, which changes a mind rather than revealing one.

lib-peme-trust-childlike-faith.rationale: The target loses judgment and believes almost any lie - diminishing the single mental capability of judgment, matching peme-4b 'Diminish a single mental capability in a person', not peme-4a (memory removal) or peme-4c (blunting emotions).

lib-peme-enchantment-detachment.rationale: Calms and greatly lowers the intensity of the target's current emotions, matching peme-4c 'Reduce the intensity of all of a person's emotions' verbatim, not peme-4a (memory) or peme-4b (a single mental capability).

lib-peme-loss-but-moments-memory.rationale: Removes up to five continuous minutes from a target's memory - a short/minor memory, matching peme-10a 'Remove a minor or short memory from a person's mind', not peme-10b's reduction of all mental capabilities.

lib-peme-black-whisper.rationale: The target must resist or 'go completely insane', matching peme-15c 'Drive a person insane' verbatim, not peme-15a (a major memory) or peme-15b (removing all emotions).

lib-peme-blessing-childlike-bliss.rationale: Reduces an adult mind to a child's level across the board (solving problems, reasoning, expressing emotion), matching peme-10b 'Reduce all of a person's mental capabilities', not peme-10a's single-memory removal.

lib-peme-passions-lost-feeling.rationale: The target is unable to feel any sort of emotion, matching peme-15b 'Remove all emotions from a person' verbatim, not peme-15a (a major memory) or peme-15c (driving someone insane).

lib-peme-poisoning-will.rationale: Gradually saps will and vitality, dulling caring and passion broadly across everyone in the cursed area, matching peme-4c 'Reduce the intensity of all of a person's emotions' - not a single capability (peme-4b) or a removed memory (peme-4a).

lib-reme-aura-rightful-authority.rationale: The target is strongly inclined to obey the caster as a natural superior, matching reme-5c 'Incline a person to a particular sort of response' - not reme-5a (controlling an emotion the target must already feel) or reme-5b (controlling a disembodied spirit; the target here is a living person).

lib-reme-coerce-spirits-night.rationale: Makes a ghost obey the caster's threats - the target is explicitly a disembodied spirit, matching reme-5b 'Control a disembodied spirit associated with Mentem', not reme-5a (a natural emotion) or reme-5c (inclining a person's response).

lib-reme-visions-infernal-terrors.rationale: Causes everything the target sees and hears to be colored with terror, affecting the target's reactions across the board (per the Stamina-roll effect table), matching reme-10b 'Imbue all of a person's responses with a particular emotion' - not reme-10a's active control of one cultivated emotion.

lib-rean-ward-against-beasts-legend.rationale: Its prose reads 'No magical beast whose Magic Might is equal to or less than the level can affect anyone within the Circle', so the warded class is beasts of the Magic realm that carry Might. rean-gen-2 is 'Create a circle warding against animals from one realm (Divine, Faerie, Infernal, or Magic) with Might less than or equal to the level of the spell (Touch, Ring, Circle)', and this art's own drafting treats 'beast' and 'animal' as the same word — Circle of Beast Warding ('a circle that no normal beast will cross') is built on the level-2 bullet 'Protect the target from animal attacks (only affects animals without supernatural abilities)', so a 'magical beast' is that same class with supernatural abilities. rean-gen is the near miss and is excluded because it wards 'beings associated with Animal', which rean-gen-2's own note says is a different class ('Note that animals are not necessarily associated with Animal, or vice versa'); this spell states no Form association at all, only that the target is a beast and that its Might is Magic.

lib-reme-ring-warding-against-spirits.rationale: Its prose reads 'Only ghosts and spirits with current Magic Might higher than the spell's level can enter the ring you create' and 'This spell does not affect ghosts or spirits associated with the other realms' — the one restriction it states is realm, and the warded class is spirits as such. reme-G2 is 'Ward against spirits belonging to one realm (Divine, Faerie, Infernal, or Magic) with a Might less than or equal to the level of the spell (Touch, Ring, Circle)', which is that scope exactly. reme-G is the near miss and is excluded because it wards 'beings associated with Mentem': the same Rego Mentem table writes 'Control a disembodied spirit associated with Mentem, such as most ghosts' (level 5) and 'Summon a disembodied spirit associated with Mentem, such as a ghost' (level 15), and Rego Animal writes 'Control a disembodied spirit associated with Animal', so in this book 'spirit' is a category that takes a Form qualifier rather than being a Mentem qualifier itself — and this spell prints no such qualifier where the table would print one.

lib-crvi-restore-faded-threads.rationale: Its prose reads 'This spell temporarily restores spell traces to a fresh state (as if they had just expired). The spell will restore spell traces of negative magnitude up to the magnitude of this spell –3.' crvi-G4 is the only one of the four Creo Vim General bullets about traces — 'Refreshes all spell traces within the target that are less than the magnitude of the guideline –1, in negative magnitude (this restores them to their initial strength, generally half the magnitude of the spell)' — and its arithmetic lands exactly: the design line (Base, +1 Touch, +1 Dia) puts the guideline two magnitudes below the spell, so 'the magnitude of the guideline –1' is 'the magnitude of this spell –3'. crvi-G2 is the nearest rejected candidate, being the other bullet that turns on Intellego investigation of magic, but it 'prevents Intellego spells ... from learning any details about the magic on the target' — this spell exists to make the traces examinable, which is the opposite; crvi-G1 and crvi-G3 are likewise concealment shells, not restorations.

lib-crvi-shell-false-determinations.rationale: Its prose reads 'All attempts to investigate the magic item give false information about its powers unless half of the level of the shell is exceeded by the magus's Investigation roll.' crvi-G3 is 'Create a magical shell which gives false information about the target to Intellego spells with level less than or equal to half its level plus one magnitude' — the only bullet that supplies false information, and the only one whose threshold is halved, matching the printed 'half of the level of the shell' (with (Base effect, +1 Touch), half the guideline plus one magnitude is half the shell's own level). crvi-G1 is the near miss and is excluded by its own parenthetical: 'this aura is generic magic only — no misleading information can be supplied'. crvi-G2's threshold is the full level, which is Shell of Opaque Mysteries, not this spell; crvi-G4 is about spell traces.

lib-crvi-shell-opaque-mysteries.rationale: Its prose reads 'it causes all attempts to investigate the magic item to utterly fail, unless the level of the ritual is exceeded by the magus's Investigation roll.' crvi-G2 is 'Create a magical shell which prevents Intellego spells with a level less than or equal to its level, plus one magnitude from learning any details about the magic on the target' — learning no details at all is 'utterly fail', and the threshold is the full level of the ritual, exactly as printed (with (Base effect, +1 Touch), the guideline plus one magnitude is the ritual's own level). crvi-G3 is the near miss — the entry itself says this spell is 'similar to Shell of False Determinations' — and is excluded twice over: it 'gives false information about the target', which this spell explicitly does not do, and its threshold is half the level rather than 'the level of the ritual'. crvi-G1 supplies a merely generic aura and crvi-G4 is about spell traces.

lib-muvi-mirror-opposition-form.rationale: Its prose reads 'this causes the targeted spell to have the exact opposite of its normal effects. This effect works on spells up to half the (level – 5) of the Mirror of Opposition spell', with the worked example inverting 'a Momentary Perdo Corpus spell' into 'probably a Creo Corpus spell of Sun duration'. muvi-G3 is 'Totally change a spell of less than or equal to half the (level + 1 magnitude) of the Vim spell (this may change the Technique, Form, or both of the target spell, and needs no requisites for those Arts)'; with (Base effect, +2 Voice) the guideline sits two magnitudes below the spell, so 'half the (guideline + 1 magnitude)' is 'half the (level – 5)' exactly as printed. muvi-G2 is the near miss and is excluded because it 'may not change either the Technique or Form of the target spell', and Perdo Corpus becoming Creo Corpus is a Technique change; muvi-G1 is excluded because it 'may not change the primary effect of the spell', which inversion is.

lib-muvi-shroud-magic.rationale: Its prose reads 'This spell allows a magus to suppress or alter the sigil in a spell that is currently being cast. The spell to be shrouded can be up to double the Shroud's level.' muvi-G1 is 'Superficially change a spell of less than or equal to twice the (level + 1 magnitude) of the Vim spell (this may not change the primary effect of the spell, or its power)'; with (Base effect, +1 Touch) the guideline is one magnitude below the spell, so twice (guideline + 1 magnitude) is exactly 'double the Shroud's level', and a sigil is neither the primary effect nor the power, so muvi-G1's restriction is satisfied rather than violated. muvi-G2 is the near miss and is excluded arithmetically: its cap is the guideline + 1 magnitude, i.e. the Shroud's own level, not double it. muvi-G3 would cap at half that again.

lib-muvi-sorcerers-fork.rationale: Its prose reads 'This spell splits another spell (whose level must be less than or equal to the level of this spell) into two or more identical spells of reduced power ... the power of the effect is divided by the number of resulting split spells.' muvi-G2 is 'Significantly change a spell of less than or equal to the level + 1 magnitude of the Vim spell (this may not change either the Technique or Form of the target spell; a change in power of plus or minus one magnitude is a significant change, as is a change of target if the target was possible for the original spell)': with (Base effect, +1 Touch) that cap is the Fork's own level as printed, the Technique and Form are untouched, and both a reduction in power and a change of target are the bullet's own examples of significance. muvi-G1 is the near miss and is excluded because a superficial change 'may not change the primary effect of the spell, or its power', and dividing the power is what the Fork does; it would also allow double the Fork's level, which the prose forbids.

lib-muvi-wizards-boost-form.rationale: Its prose reads 'You cast this spell as another spell of a level less than or equal to this one is cast. The effect of the other spell increases 5 levels in power, but not past the level of the Wizard's Boost.' Five levels is one magnitude, and muvi-G2 names that case outright — 'Significantly change a spell of less than or equal to the level + 1 magnitude of the Vim spell (... a change in power of plus or minus one magnitude is a significant change)' — while with (Base effect, +1 Touch) its cap is the Boost's own level, exactly the printed 'less than or equal to this one'. muvi-G1 is the near miss and is excluded because a superficial change 'may not change the primary effect of the spell, or its power', and raising the target's power is the entire spell. muvi-G3 is excluded by its halved cap and because no Technique or Form changes.

lib-muvi-wizards-reach-form.rationale: Its prose reads 'The range of the targeted spell increases by one category. You may not affect a single spell more than once with this spell, and the targeted spell must be at least one magnitude lower in level than this spell.' With (Base effect, +2 Voice) the guideline sits two magnitudes below the spell, so muvi-G2's cap of 'the level + 1 magnitude of the Vim spell' is precisely one magnitude below the Reach's own level, matching the printed restriction; and changing a spell's Range is the same order of alteration muvi-G2 calls significant ('as is a change of target if the target was possible for the original spell'), with Technique and Form untouched. muvi-G1 is the near miss and is excluded arithmetically: twice (guideline + 1 magnitude) is roughly double the Reach's level, an order of magnitude away from the printed cap of one magnitude below it. muvi-G3 caps at about a quarter of the Reach's level and permits Technique/Form changes this spell does not make.

lib-pevi-demons-eternal-oblivion.rationale: Its prose reads 'Weakens and possibly destroys a creature with Infernal Might. If the spell penetrates the creature's Magic Resistance, the creature loses Might Score equal to the spell's level.' pevi-G3 is 'Reduce a target's Might Score by the level of the spell + 2 magnitudes, as long as the spell penetrates the creature's Magic Resistance'; with (Base effect, +2 Voice) the guideline plus two magnitudes is the spell's own level, so the reduction is 'equal to the spell's level' exactly as printed, and the Penetration proviso is quoted almost verbatim. pevi-G4 is the near miss — same arithmetic, same Penetration clause — and is excluded on the one word that separates the two rows: pevi-G4 reduces the 'Might Pool', and this spell's prose says 'Might Score'. No other candidate reduces Might at all; the twelve others dispel, conceal, destroy vis, or reduce casting totals.

lib-pevi-disenchant.rationale: Its prose reads 'You make a Hermetic magic item lose all its powers permanently if the level of this spell + a stress die (no botch) equals or exceeds the highest level of the enchantments in the item', and its stat line prints 'Ritual'. pevi-G9 is 'Dispel a Hermetic enchantment with a level less than the guideline level used + 1 magnitude + a stress die (no botch); the spell must be a Ritual'. pevi-G10 is the near miss and is the *only* other candidate that is also enchantment-specific and also Ritual-required, so neither of those properties discriminates. What does is that pevi-G10 'must specify a particular Hermetic Form or a specific type of enchantment such as Talismans, Familiars or Longevity Rituals', and Disenchant specifies none -- it strips whatever the item has. Its threshold also differs (twice the guideline + 2 magnitudes, against the printed spell level + a stress die). Rationale corrected under item 32.2: it previously called pevi-G9 the only enchantment-specific Ritual row of the thirteen, which is false, though the discriminator it then gave was the right one.

lib-pevi-masking-odor-magic.rationale: Its prose reads 'Prevents the detection of a magic spell, or of a magic power in an item or being, by InVi magic, unless the level of the InVi spell exceeds twice the level of this spell – 5 (for example, exceeds 20 for a level 15 version).' pevi-G1 is 'Make something (including a magical item) seem non-magical to any Intellego spell of less than or equal to twice the (level + 2 magnitudes) of this spell' — the only one of the thirteen bullets about concealment rather than destruction, and the arithmetic checks out: with (Base effect, +1 Touch, +2 Sun) the guideline sits three magnitudes below, so twice (guideline + 2 magnitudes) is twice (this spell's level – 5), which is 20 for the level 15 version the prose itself cites. pevi-G2 looks like the near miss only in the catalog's compressed description ('Dispel specific effect type with Intellego spell'); the rulebook row mentions no Intellego at all — it reads 'Dispel effects of a specific type with a level less than or equal to the level + 4 magnitudes of the Vim spell + a stress die (no botch)' — and Masking dispels nothing, it hides.

lib-pevi-unravelling-fabric-form.rationale: Its prose reads 'This spell will cancel the effects of any one spell of a specified Form whose level is less than or equal to (spell level + 10 + stress die (no botch)). There are 10 variants that cover each Hermetic Form.' pevi-G2 is 'Dispel effects of a specific type with a level less than or equal to the level + 4 magnitudes of the Vim spell + a stress die (no botch); a specific type could be Hermetic Terram magic, or Shamanic spirit control magic' — 'a specified Form' is that row's own example of a specific type, and with (Base effect, +2 Voice) guideline + 4 magnitudes is the spell's level + 10, matching the printed formula term for term. pevi-G5 is the near miss and is excluded twice: it dispels 'any supernatural effect of one realm', which is a realm restriction rather than the Form restriction this spell prints, and its threshold is halved — half the (spell level + 10 + stress die) rather than the printed spell level + 10 + stress die. pevi-G9/G10 are enchantment-and-Ritual rows and this spell is neither.

lib-pevi-wind-mundane-silence.rationale: Its prose reads 'You raise a metaphorical "breeze" that blows the magic away from an area, canceling the effects of any spell there. You can cancel the effects of any spell if, with this spell, you can double the level of the spell on a stress die + the level of your spell' — that is, the target spell's level may be at most half of (this spell's level + a stress die). pevi-G5 is 'Dispel any supernatural effect of one realm with a level less than or equal to half the (level + 4 magnitudes + a stress die (no botch)) of the Vim spell'; with (Base effect, +2 Voice, +2 Room) the guideline sits four magnitudes below, so 'guideline + 4 magnitudes' is the spell's own level and the row reduces to half (this spell's level + a stress die), exactly the printed rule. pevi-G2 is the near miss and is excluded on both counts: it needs 'effects of a specific type', where the Wind cancels 'any spell there' with no type named, and its threshold is not halved. The Vim preamble also assigns this spell to pevi-G5's side of the enchantment line: 'Wind of Mundane Silence could dispel a stone wall produced by a magical item, but Disenchant is needed to dispel the magic of the item itself.'

lib-revi-circular-ward-against-demons.rationale: Its prose reads 'All creatures with Infernal Might equal to or less than the level of the spell are unable to enter the circle or harm those within it.' revi-G1 is 'Ward against all supernatural beings from one realm (Divine, Faerie, Infernal, or Magic) with Might less than or equal to the level of the spell (Touch, Ring, Circle)' — the only one of the five Rego Vim General bullets whose subject is beings rather than spells, and whose printed reference parameters are this spell's own R: Touch, D: Ring, T: Circle, which is why the design line is a bare '(Base spell)' with nothing to charge. revi-G2 is the nearest rejected candidate and is excluded because it sustains or suppresses 'a spell you have cast'; this ward's target is a demon's Might, not a spell, and against revi-G2's Personal/Momentary/Individual reference the Touch/Ring/Circle stat line would owe magnitudes that the printed design line does not charge.

lib-revi-maintaining-demanding-spell.rationale: Its prose reads 'You cast this spell on a spell that you have already cast and are maintaining through concentration. The spell that requires concentration is then automatically maintained for the duration of this spell ... This spell only works on spells of equal or lower level.' revi-G2 is 'Sustain or suppress a spell you have cast whose level is less than or equal to the level + 2 magnitudes of the Vim spell (this cannot make a spell last longer than it could have naturally, so the sustaining version is only useful with Concentration Duration among standard Hermetic Durations)' — the parenthetical describes this spell's use case exactly, and with (Base effect, +1 Touch, +1 Diam) the guideline + 2 magnitudes is the spell's own level, matching 'equal or lower level'. revi-G4 is the near miss and is excluded because it is for 'a spell cast by another', where this one is cast on a spell you have already cast yourself; its cap would also be halved. revi-G5 adds 'of a specific type', which this spell does not specify.

lib-revi-opening-intangible-tunnel.rationale: Its prose reads 'You can open a magical channel from yourself to some target, allowing you to cast any spell with a range greater than Personal on that target ... Spells cast through the tunnel cannot be of higher level than that of this spell.' revi-G3 is 'Create a conduit or container for spells with level less than or equal to the level + 5 magnitudes of the Vim spell (a conduit puts you in mystical contact with the target at effective Touch range, while a container holds a spell for a specific length of time before releasing it)' — the conduit half of that clause is this spell's own description, and with (Base effect, +4 Arc, +1 Conc) the guideline + 5 magnitudes is the spell's own level, matching the printed cap. revi-G4 is the near miss because it carries the same '+5 magnitudes' term, but it 'sustains or suppresses a spell cast by another' and the tunnel neither sustains nor suppresses anything; its cap is halved besides, which the printed cap contradicts.

lib-revi-suppressing-wizards-handiwork.rationale: Its prose reads 'Cancels one spell that you have cast, but only as long as you concentrate. When concentration is broken the effects of the spell return ... The level of the spell to be suppressed must be less than or equal to the level of this spell.' revi-G2 is 'Sustain or suppress a spell you have cast whose level is less than or equal to the level + 2 magnitudes of the Vim spell (... a suppressed spell still ends when its original duration expires)'; with (Base, +1 Touch, +1 Conc) the guideline + 2 magnitudes is the spell's own level, matching the printed cap, and 'a spell you have cast' matches 'one spell that you have cast'. revi-G4 is the near miss and is excluded by 'cast by another' plus its halved cap; revi-G5 is excluded because it is also 'cast by another' and further requires spells 'of a specific type', where this spell suppresses any one of your own.

lib-muau-infernal-smoke-death.rationale: Turns normal smoke into a corrosive cloud that inflicts +25 damage on anyone immersed in it, matching muau-gen 'transform air into a gas doing +level damage' verbatim (base 25 = +25 damage), not muau-gen-2 which drains an air elemental's Might pool and has nothing to do with smoke or damage to bystanders.

lib-crvi-enigmas-gift.rationale: Gives the target Warping Points from a burst of magic, matching crvi-5a 'create a burst of magic that gives the target Warping Points' verbatim, not crvi-5b which slows the decay rate of an Arcane Connection and has nothing to do with granting Warping.

lib-peig-wizards-icy-grip.rationale: Chills a person and deals damage that scales with the spell's level, matching peig-5b 'chill a person, taking damage that scales with the spell's level' verbatim, not peig-5a which strongly chills an object (e.g. freezing water) rather than harming a person.

lib-craq-deluge-rushing-and-dashing.rationale: Causes a stream to overflow into a raging, damaging torrent, matching craq-10a 'create a geyser with a very high rate of flow' -- a forceful creation of moving water. craq-10b creates a poison causing a Medium Wound; the spell's own text never mentions poison.

lib-reaq-ice-drowning.rationale: Drives ice chunks to pound against anything on the water's surface, matching reaq-5b 'control a liquid in a violent way'. Not reaq-5a (warding against mundane water -- this spell attacks, not wards), reaq-5c (no disembodied spirit involved) or reaq-5d (no water elemental involved).

lib-inme-frosty-breath-spoken-lie.rationale: Determines whether a spoken statement is a lie, matching inme-10b 'discover the truth of a statement' verbatim. Not inme-10a (sensing emotions) -- the spell's own text is about truthfulness, not emotional state.

lib-reaq-break-oncoming-wave.rationale: The spell's own design line says 'ward, so the target is the warded Individual, not the water', matching reaq-5a 'ward against mundane water' by name -- the only warding candidate of the four. Not reaq-5b (control a liquid violently -- this spell blocks water, it doesn't move it), reaq-5c (no disembodied spirit involved) or reaq-5d (no water elemental involved). The 'mundane' qualifier is looser than the spell's own 'including magical ones', the same tolerated description-vs-spell mismatch as elsewhere in this ledger (see item 32).

lib-inte-tracks-faerie-glow.rationale: The spell gets one kind of information -- where a specific being passed -- and presents it in a non-obvious way, as a faint light on the tracks themselves. That presentation is what makes it look like a 'learn a property' effect, but what the magic delivers is the tracks together with the ground they sit in, which is inte-4b's 'See an object and its surroundings'; the printed Target is Vision. The entry previously read inte-4a and argued 'no seeing is involved' -- contradicted by the spell's own text, which is about tracks that 'stand out' to the eye and about 'Tracking at night without a light source'. Corrected under item 32.2 on the user's ruling, together with lib-inte-sense-feet-that-tread-earth; lib-inte-eyes-eons keeps inte-4a, where a single mundane property really is all that is learned.

lib-inte-sense-feet-that-tread-earth.rationale: One kind of information, delivered through an unexpected sense: you touch the earth and perceive the things moving on it, which is inte-4b's 'See an object and its surroundings' with the ground as the surroundings. The listed facts -- direction, distance, weight, number, manner of movement -- are aspects of perceiving those things where they are, not five separately-learned properties; reading them as properties would put the spell on the *level 10* row ('Learn all the natural properties of an object'), and it is printed at base 4. The entry previously read inte-4a and leaned on the spell's verb being 'feel' rather than 'see', which mistakes the sense used for the kind of information got. Corrected under item 32.2 on the user's ruling, together with lib-inte-tracks-faerie-glow.

lib-mute-crystal-dart.rationale: 'Transforms a stone into a 10-inch crystal dart' is a solid-to-solid change within the earth/mineral family -- the only one of the level-3 guidelines built for that axis at all. Not mute-3a (slightly unnatural dirt: a state-of-being change, not a change of material) or mute-3b (dirt into liquid or gas: wrong state of matter entirely, and this dart is solid). The design line's own material-adjustment note ('to change to or from stone or glass, add one magnitude; to change to or from metal or gemstone, add two magnitudes') has no such extra magnitude in the design line (Base 3, +2 Voice, +1 Rego requisite sums to exactly the printed level 10 with nothing to spare) -- so the transformation must be one the guideline already prices at base 3 without surcharge, which is mute-3c's own named 'dirt to stone, or vice versa' pair. The Rego requisite is for the dart's flight and strike (Req: Rego, matching 'floats into the air, and speeds off like an arrow'), not for the material change, so it does not bear on this choice.

lib-crig-ball-abysmal-flame.rationale: New ambiguity surfaced by item 29's semicolon fix (the design line was previously unparseable). The spell's own text states the effect in the guideline's own words: 'A ball of flame shoots from your hand to strike a single target, doing +30 damage' matches crig-25a ('Create a fire doing +30 damage') on the exact damage figure. crig-25b ('Create a fire elemental from a base amount of elemental matter') is a different effect entirely -- an elemental, not a damaging bolt -- and is independently ruled out: its own catalog entry is Ritual-only (ritualRequirement: required), but Ball of Abysmal Flame's stat line (R: Voice, D: Mom, T: Ind) carries no Ritual marker at all. Both the description and the Ritual constraint force crig-25a; nothing about the spell supports crig-25b.

lib-crhe-bountiful-feast.rationale: The design line's own parenthetical says the +1 Size token is 'for a total of +4 Size, including the +3 from the guideline' -- crhe-1a is the only one of the five candidates whose description states a baked-in Size enhancement at all ('includes a +3 Size enhancement'), so the design line's own arithmetic forces this pick, not just prose similarity. Not crhe-1b/1c (create a product/plant -- this spell doesn't create anything, it protects existing crops), 1d (prevent sickness -- narrower than the spell's own 'healthier, larger, and tastier') or 1e (heal a wound -- no wound involved).

lib-pean-revenge-bitten-toad.rationale: Its prose reads 'Any creatures who bite (or otherwise taste) the caster suffer a Heavy Wound' -- verbatim the guideline 'Inflict a Heavy Wound'. Not a destroyed sense, a crippled limb, or ageing.

lib-crme-scent-predator.rationale: Its prose reads 'Anyone smelling the caster is struck by an overwhelming sensation of menace and hostility' -- an emotion placed into a mind, not a memory restored to a fresh state.

lib-reco-marking-territory.rationale: The design line glosses its own base: '(Base 3 [move in direction "away"], +2 Ring, +2 Scent)'. That is 'Move a target slowly in one direction', not a minor symptom of disease.

lib-mume-clarion-call-war-horse.rationale: Its prose reads 'Anyone hearing the caster's battle cry is heartened by its tone, and receives a +3 bonus to his Brave Personality Trait' -- a major change to emotion, not to a memory of a series of events.

lib-crig-brilliance-eagles-plumage.rationale: Its prose reads 'blinded by the brilliant light shining from his body' -- 'Create light as bright as direct sunlight on a clear day'. The spell creates no fire, ignites nothing, and heats nothing.

lib-peme-closed-mouth-nightwalker.rationale: Its prose reads 'Anyone seeing the caster instantly forgets that he did so' -- one brief memory removed, not a reduction of all the target's mental capabilities.

lib-muan-voice-bjornaer-magus.rationale: The caster stays the same animal and gains a human voice: 'it targets the vocal capacity of that form'. That is 'Change an animal in a minor way so that it is no longer natural', not a change into a different animal, and the target is a living beast rather than animal products.

lib-muan-form-temperament-heartbeast.rationale: Same reading as The Voice of the Bjornaer Magus: the animal is unchanged and its temperament correspondences are unnaturally enhanced ('they enhance the correspondences to the temperament of that form'). A minor unnatural change to an animal.

lib-peme-embrace-boethius.rationale: Its prose reads 'destroying a part of his understanding of formulaic spell casting' -- a major, long memory removed. It removes no emotions and drives nobody insane.

lib-muvi-facilitate-stifled-form-spell.rationale: The spell removes the casting penalty for reduced or absent gestures and voice, leaving the targeted spell otherwise intact -- a superficial change. Its prose's ceiling, a target 'whose level must be less than twice the level of this spell', matches G1's doubling tier rather than G2's or G3's tighter ones.

lib-pevi-roosters-crow.rationale: **The spell's own text does not discriminate, and this entry rests on analogy.** It reads 'Any demons who hear the caster's shout lose Might equal to the spell's (level - 5)' -- 'Might', with neither 'Score' nor 'Pool', which is the single word separating pevi-G3 from pevi-G4. The arithmetic fits both identically: with (Base effect, +3 Sound) the guideline sits three magnitudes below, so guideline + 2 magnitudes is the spell's level - 5, exactly as printed. Two supports for pevi-G3 (Score). First, Demon's Eternal Oblivion is the established core parallel -- same formula shape, same Penetration proviso -- and says 'loses Might Score' outright; this ledger resolves it to pevi-G3. Second, a Might Pool reduction is temporary: 'Might Pools almost always refresh to the creature's Might Score over the course of a day' (Core Rules line 17831), so pevi-G4 would make a Momentary shout a debuff lasting until the demon rests, where the spell reads as weakening demons. Neither support is forced by the text. Recorded as analogy-based under item 32.2, where a blind model pass reached pevi-G3 by the same route and flagged the entry ambiguous -- correctly.
